revisions.title: When polish begins to persuade
revisions.body: Phaedrus's performance keeps presentation and content distinct: its polished delivery can be playful while the seriousness of what it says remains a separate question. The passage thus leaves style and substance to be assessed separately.

revisions.title: The lover's discipline
revisions.body: Here the lover's relation is disciplined by a model: he honors and imitates the god whose chorus he followed, fashions the beloved toward that image, and must govern opposed horses—one yielding to word, the other only reluctantly to whip and goad. The test is therefore what kind of relation desire can sustain: one ordered by guidance, not mere force.
